items.stem: Historians debate whether the Allied strategy of "unconditional surrender" prolonged WWII by eliminating incentives for Germany and Japan to negotiate peace. Evaluate this debate by examining evidence from BOTH the European and Pacific theaters. Was unconditional surrender the right policy?
items.stemEs: Los historiadores debaten si la estrategia aliada de "rendición incondicional" prolongó la SGMM al eliminar incentivos para que Alemania y Japón negociaran la paz. Evalúe este debate.
items.correctAnswer: Strong responses should present arguments for and against unconditional surrender with theater-specific evidence. For: prevented a repeat of WWI's ambiguous ending, ensured complete denazification, allowed total reconstruction. Against: may have stiffened German resistance, complicated peace feelers from anti-Hitler Germans, may have delayed Japanese surrender. Students should recognize the counterfactual nature of the debate.
items.explanation: A strong response should weigh arguments from both the European and Pacific theaters, including whether unconditional surrender prevented a negotiated escape for Axis leaders or instead ensured total defeat of militarist regimes. It needs evidence from both Germany and Japan before reaching a clear judgment about whether the policy was justified. The question matters because war aims can shape how long a conflict lasts and what kind of peace follows.
items.explanationEs: Este ítem DOK 4 requiere evaluar un debate de política histórica a través de dos teatros y construir una posición matizada.

items.stem:
Read the following two primary source excerpts and answer the prompt below.

─────────────────────────────────────────
DOCUMENT A
Calvin Coolidge, address to the American Society of Newspaper Editors, Washington, D.C., January 17, 1925 (White House press release / Congressional Record, public domain):

"The chief business of the American people is business. They are profoundly concerned with producing, buying, selling, investing and prospering in the world…Advertising ministers to the spiritual side of trade. It is a great power that has been entrusted to your keeping which charges you with the high responsibility of inspiring and ennobling the commercial motives and ideals of America."

─────────────────────────────────────────
DOCUMENT B
U.S. Senate Banking and Currency Committee Report on the Stock Market Crash, 1931 (U.S. Government Printing Office, public domain):

"The decade of the nineteen-twenties saw a vast increase in the use of credit for the purchase of securities…The very ease with which credit was obtained, the persistently advancing prices of securities, and the large profits made by those who bought on margin all combined to attract new participants into the market…When the collapse came, it came with a completeness and a speed that took even the most experienced observers by surprise."

─────────────────────────────────────────
Using BOTH documents and your knowledge of mass media and consumer culture (US.34) and economic prosperity and speculation (US.36), write a multi-paragraph response that applies HIPP to each document and constructs an argument about how the consumer culture promoted in the 1920s created the conditions for economic collapse. Your response must analyze both documents' Historical context, Intended audience, Purpose, and Point of view; explain what each document's perspective reveals about its author's knowledge and interests; and use outside evidence to support your argument.
items.stemEs:
Lee los siguientes dos extractos de fuentes primarias y responde al ejercicio.

─────────────────────────────────────────
DOCUMENTO A
Calvin Coolidge, discurso ante la Sociedad Estadounidense de Editores de Periódicos, Washington, D.C., 17 de enero de 1925 (comunicado de prensa de la Casa Blanca / Registro del Congreso, dominio público):

"El principal negocio del pueblo americano es el negocio. Están profundamente preocupados por producir, comprar, vender, invertir y prosperar en el mundo…La publicidad sirve al lado espiritual del comercio. Es un gran poder que ha sido encomendado a su cuidado, lo que les carga con la alta responsabilidad de inspirar y ennoblecer los motivos e ideales comerciales de América."

─────────────────────────────────────────
DOCUMENTO B
Informe del Comité de Banca y Moneda del Senado de EE. UU. sobre el Colapso de la Bolsa de Valores, 1931 (Imprenta del Gobierno de EE. UU., dominio público):

"La década de los años 1920 vio un vasto aumento en el uso del crédito para la compra de valores…La misma facilidad con que se obtenía crédito, los precios persistentemente en alza de los valores y las grandes ganancias obtenidas por quienes compraron con margen combinaron para atraer nuevos participantes al mercado…Cuando llegó el colapso, llegó con una completitud y una velocidad que tomó por sorpresa incluso a los observadores más experimentados."

─────────────────────────────────────────
Usando AMBOS documentos y tu conocimiento de los medios masivos y la cultura del consumidor (US.34) y la prosperidad económica y la especulación (US.36), escribe una respuesta de varios párrafos que aplique HIPP a cada documento y construya un argumento sobre cómo la cultura consumista promovida en los años 1920 creó las condiciones para el colapso económico. Tu respuesta debe analizar el Contexto histórico, la Audiencia prevista, el Propósito y el Punto de vista de ambos documentos; explicar qué revela la perspectiva de cada documento sobre el conocimiento e intereses de su autor; y usar evidencia externa para apoyar tu argumento.
items.correctAnswer: A top-score response (6/6) will: (1) HIPP on Document A: Historical context—mid-1920s prosperity, Coolidge pro-business ideology; Intended audience—newspaper editors (gatekeepers of advertising revenue and public opinion); Purpose—legitimate consumer culture and advertising as morally noble, aligning business success with spiritual virtue; Point of view—president invested in the legitimacy of laissez-faire capitalism with a significant limitation: speaking in 1925, Coolidge has no knowledge of the 1929 collapse and has every incentive to celebrate the economy. (2) HIPP on Document B: Historical context—Senate investigation AFTER the 1929 crash; Intended audience—senators and the American public seeking explanations; Purpose—identify systemic causes of the crash (credit, margin buying) to inform potential regulation; Point of view—retrospective legislative investigators who can now see the crash's causes with hindsight. (3) Argument: Document A shows the ideological fuel for the crash—Coolidge's equation of advertising and investment with spiritual virtue encouraged reckless participation in credit-fueled speculation. Document B shows the structural mechanism. Together they indict laissez-faire ideology and media culture as enabling conditions for the Depression. (4) Outside evidence: installment buying, radio advertising, prosperity rhetoric vs. agricultural depression, Black Tuesday, margin buying mechanics, Smoot-Hawley tariff, Mellon tax policy.
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize across multiple standards and sources, constructing an extended argument that connects US.34, US.36, US.35 through evidence-based reasoning requiring sustained analytical writing.
items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (6 points):
6 - Exemplary: Full HIPP for both documents including Coolidge's limitation (he cannot foresee the crash) and Senate Committee's retrospective advantage. Precise argument linking consumer culture ideology (Doc A) to structural vulnerability (Doc B). At least two pieces of outside evidence. Cross-era connection to Great Depression.
5 - Advanced: HIPP (3+ elements) for both. Clear argument. Both documents cited. At least one piece of outside evidence.
4 - Proficient: HIPP (2+ elements) for both. Argument present. Both documents used.
3 - Adequate: Some HIPP for both. Argument present but underdeveloped.
2 - Developing: HIPP for only one document. Weak argument.
1 - Beginning: Summary without HIPP. No clear argument.
0 - No response or completely off-topic.

DOCUMENT ANALYSIS EXPECTATIONS: Coolidge's 'limitation' (no foreknowledge of crash); Senate Committee's retrospective position; both documents produced in very different political contexts.
KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Installment buying, radio/advertising, margin buying, Black Tuesday, Mellon tax policy, Smoot-Hawley, Hoover's response, connection to US.39 Great Depression.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (6 puntos):
6 - Ejemplar: HIPP completo para ambos documentos, incluyendo la limitación de Coolidge (no puede prever el colapso) y la ventaja retrospectiva del Comité del Senado. Argumento preciso que vincula la ideología de la cultura consumista (Doc A) con la vulnerabilidad estructural (Doc B). Al menos dos piezas de evidencia externa. Conexión entre eras con la Gran Depresión.
5 - Avanzado: HIPP (3+ elementos) para ambos. Argumento claro. Ambos documentos citados. Al menos una pieza de evidencia externa.
4 - Competente: HIPP (2+ elementos) para ambos. Argumento presente. Ambos documentos utilizados.
3 - Adecuado: Cierto HIPP para ambos. Argumento presente pero poco desarrollado.
2 - En desarrollo: HIPP para solo un documento. Argumento débil.
1 - Inicial: Resumen sin HIPP. Sin argumento claro.
0 - Sin respuesta o completamente fuera del tema.

EXPECTATIVAS DE ANÁLISIS DOCUMENTAL: 'Limitación' de Coolidge (sin conocimiento previo del colapso); posición retrospectiva del Comité del Senado; ambos documentos producidos en contextos políticos muy diferentes.
EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Compras a plazos, radio/publicidad, compras con margen, Martes Negro, política fiscal de Mellon, Smoot-Hawley, respuesta de Hoover, conexión con US.39 Gran Depresión.

items.stem: Historians have long debated the relationship between the prosperity and cultural optimism of the 1920s and the economic collapse of 1929. Using your knowledge of mass media and consumer culture (US.34), economic prosperity and speculation (US.36), and the political philosophy of Return to Normalcy under Harding and Coolidge (US.35), write an extended essay that argues whether the conditions that produced the Great Depression were already embedded in the prosperity of the 1920s or were the result of unforeseen shocks and policy failures. Your essay must: (1) state a clear, defensible thesis about the relationship between 1920s prosperity and the seeds of economic collapse; (2) use specific evidence from all three standards to support your thesis — including how mass media shaped consumer behavior, how speculation and credit use changed the economy, and how government policy under Harding and Coolidge either enabled or failed to check these trends; (3) acknowledge and respond to the strongest counterargument to your thesis; and (4) synthesize across the unit to connect 1920s economic and political choices to the onset of the Great Depression (Unit 5). Your essay should be 4–6 well-developed paragraphs.
items.stemEs: Los historiadores han debatido durante mucho tiempo la relación entre la prosperidad y el optimismo cultural de los años 1920 y el colapso económico de 1929. Usando tu conocimiento de los medios masivos y la cultura de consumo (US.34), la prosperidad económica y la especulación (US.36) y la filosofía política del Regreso a la Normalidad bajo Harding y Coolidge (US.35), escribe un ensayo extendido que argumente si las condiciones que produjeron la Gran Depresión ya estaban incorporadas en la prosperidad de los años 1920 o fueron el resultado de choques imprevistos y fallas de política. Tu ensayo debe: (1) expresar una tesis clara y defendible sobre la relación entre la prosperidad de los años 1920 y las semillas del colapso económico; (2) usar evidencia específica de los tres estándares para apoyar tu tesis — incluyendo cómo los medios masivos moldearon el comportamiento del consumidor, cómo la especulación y el uso de crédito cambiaron la economía, y cómo la política gubernamental bajo Harding y Coolidge habilitó o no controló estas tendencias; (3) reconocer y responder al contraargumento más sólido a tu tesis; y (4) sintetizar a través de la unidad para conectar las elecciones económicas y políticas de los años 1920 con el inicio de la Gran Depresión (Unidad 5). Tu ensayo debe tener 4–6 párrafos bien desarrollados.
items.correctAnswer: A top-score response (4/4) will include: (1) A defensible thesis — e.g., 'The Great Depression was not a sudden external shock but the predictable consequence of structural weaknesses embedded in the prosperity of the 1920s: rampant speculation fueled by easy credit, a consumer economy built on advertising-driven installment buying, and a government philosophy that deliberately withdrew federal oversight of financial markets created the conditions for catastrophic collapse.' (2) Evidence from all three standards — US.34: advertising industry, radio and print advertising drove installment buying culture; consumers purchased refrigerators, automobiles, radios on credit; buying on credit meant the economy ran on debt rather than real income growth; US.36: stock market speculation on margin (buying on 10% down); speculative bubble in Florida real estate (collapsed 1926); agricultural sector already depressed throughout the 1920s — farm foreclosures widespread; income inequality masked by surface prosperity (top 1% held ~40% of wealth); US.35: Harding and Coolidge's laissez-faire philosophy, Mellon tax cuts benefiting the wealthy, Fordney-McCumber Tariff (1922) triggering European retaliatory tariffs and undermining export markets, deliberate rollback of Progressive Era regulations, Federal Reserve loose monetary policy 1924–1928. (3) Counterargument: one could argue the crash was triggered by specific Federal Reserve decisions in 1929 or unpredictable bank runs — response should explain why underlying structural fragilities made these triggers catastrophic rather than manageable. (4) Cross-unit synthesis: directly connects to the Smoot-Hawley Tariff (1930), bank failures, Hoover's response (US.39), demonstrating that Unit 4 choices created the specific vulnerabilities that turned a recession into the Great Depression.
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize across multiple standards and sources, constructing an extended argument that connects US.34, US.36, US.35 through evidence-based reasoning requiring sustained analytical writing.
items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (4 points):
4 - Exemplary: Clear, defensible thesis stated upfront. Specific evidence from all three standards (US.34, US.36, US.35) — including advertising/credit culture, margin buying, agricultural depression, Mellon tax cuts, Fordney-McCumber Tariff, and laissez-faire philosophy. Engages the counterargument substantively. Cross-unit synthesis explicitly connects 1920s choices to Great Depression onset.
3 - Proficient: Clear thesis. Specific evidence from at least two standards. Counterargument acknowledged. Some cross-unit connection to the Depression.
2 - Developing: Thesis present but underdeveloped. Evidence from one standard dominates. Counterargument absent or superficial. Limited cross-unit connection.
1 - Beginning: Vague thesis or none. Minimal evidence. No counterargument or cross-unit synthesis.
0 - No response or completely off-topic.

KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Installment buying, advertising boom, margin buying (10% down), speculative bubble, Florida real estate crash (1926), agricultural depression throughout the 1920s, income inequality (top 1%), Mellon tax cuts, Fordney-McCumber Tariff (1922), Federal Reserve loose policy, Smoot-Hawley Tariff (1930), laissez-faire philosophy.
SYNTHESIS EXPECTATIONS: Student should explicitly bridge Unit 4 (1920s prosperity) to Unit 5 (Great Depression), showing that the structural vulnerabilities created by mass consumer credit, unregulated speculation, and laissez-faire government philosophy were the causal preconditions for the economic collapse — not merely coincident background conditions.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (4 puntos):
4 - Ejemplar: Tesis clara y defendible expresada desde el inicio. Evidencia específica de los tres estándares (US.34, US.36, US.35) — incluyendo cultura de publicidad/crédito, compra con margen, depresión agrícola, recortes de impuestos de Mellon, Arancel Fordney-McCumber y filosofía de laissez-faire. Compromiso sustantivo con el contraargumento. Síntesis entre unidades que conecta explícitamente las elecciones de los años 1920 con el inicio de la Gran Depresión.
3 - Competente: Tesis clara. Evidencia específica de al menos dos estándares. Contraargumento reconocido. Alguna conexión entre unidades con la Depresión.
2 - En desarrollo: Tesis presente pero subdesarrollada. La evidencia de un estándar domina. Contraargumento ausente o superficial. Conexión limitada entre unidades.
1 - Inicial: Tesis vaga o ausente. Evidencia mínima. Sin contraargumento o síntesis entre unidades.
0 - Sin respuesta o completamente fuera del tema.

EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Compra a plazos, auge publicitario, compra con margen (10% inicial), burbuja especulativa, colapso inmobiliario de Florida (1926), depresión agrícola durante los años 1920, desigualdad de ingresos (1% superior), recortes de impuestos de Mellon, Arancel Fordney-McCumber (1922), política monetaria expansiva de la Reserva Federal, Arancel Smoot-Hawley (1930), filosofía laissez-faire.
EXPECTATIVAS DE SÍNTESIS: El estudiante debe conectar explícitamente la Unidad 4 (prosperidad de los años 1920) con la Unidad 5 (Gran Depresión), mostrando que las vulnerabilidades estructurales creadas por el crédito masivo al consumidor, la especulación no regulada y la filosofía gubernamental de laissez-faire fueron las condiciones causales previas al colapso económico.
